summary: Harbor range beacons of 1870 at Presque Isle Harbor on Lake Huron: the front tower moved into a township park; keepers from 1870, Anna Garrity 1903-1926.

structures.status: standing, moved within Range Light Park
structures.note: A 21-foot wooden tower (LighthouseFriends). The marker says it was moved near its original site in 2002.
Replaced the wooden front range light in 1967 (HMDB).

structures.type: tower on the keeper's dwelling roof
structures.note: The rear light first shone from a tower on the pitched roof of the keeper's dwelling (LighthouseFriends).
Mounted at 33 feet above the ground (LighthouseFriends). The Township museum says a tall steel tower later replaced the rear light.

staffing.note: The last keeper in the archive roster is Clement E. Richardson (1927-1929). The Township museum says it seems likely that Coast Guard personnel tended the rear light after 1939.

access.note: Range Light Park is owned by Presque Isle Township and open dawn to dusk. Neither light is open for climbing (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Presque Isle Township (park; front light); Coast Guard supervises both lights (Township museum)

events.note: Congress appropriated $7,500 for range lights marking the channel into Presque Isle Harbor. Eight and a half acres bought from Frederick Burnham for $100.
Range lights in operation by August 1870 (HMDB). The Township museum gives 1871 as the start of service ('in service 1871-present').
Isaac Coddington named first keeper on 8 September 1870 at $540 a year.
Thomas Garrity appointed third head keeper.
Patrick Garrity, Sr. became keeper, at the age of seventy-two.
Porch of the dwelling renewed; 500 feet of walk between the ranges relaid (Lighthouse Board, fiscal year 1899).
Rear light changed to show in the harbor, October 1899 (Lighthouse Board, fiscal year 1900).
Front light changed to a white flash every second, 20 September 1926. Rear light remained fixed white, now on a black pyramidal skeletal tower (LighthouseFriends).
Lights electrified and changed to fixed green (LighthouseFriends).
Front range light replaced by a light on a pole (HMDB).
Presque Isle Township acquired the front tower with state funds and private donations (HMDB).
Front tower moved near its original site; much of the lower structure rebuilt to the original plans (HMDB).
Sculpture of Anna Garrity dedicated at Presque Isle Harbor Range Light Park on 31 August 2013 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Isaac Coddington
keepers.note: Named 'Codington' by the Township museum. A Civil War veteran (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: William Sims
keepers.note: Captain William Sims, placed in charge after Coddington's death (LighthouseFriends). Wife Adeline died in 1881 and was buried along the range line.

keepers.name: Thomas Garrity
keepers.note: Assistant keeper at the new Presque Isle light under his father, then third head keeper of the range (LighthouseFriends). The Township museum says he transferred to the new light in 1891.

other_stations.name: New Presque Isle Light
other_stations.note: Assistant keeper under his father; the start year is not given.

other_stations.name: New Presque Isle Light
other_stations.note: Transferred to the new light in 1891; role not stated.

keepers.name: Patrick Garrity, Sr.
keepers.note: Keeper of the new Presque Isle light from 1871 (LighthouseFriends); range keeper from 1891 at the age of seventy-two; died in March 1903.

other_stations.name: New Presque Isle Light
other_stations.note: LighthouseFriends: moved a mile north to take charge of the new light when the old one was discontinued in 1871. The Township museum calls him keeper at the New Light.

keepers.name: Anna T. Garrity
keepers.note: Daughter of Patrick Garrity, Sr. The marker calls her one of the few women light keepers. LighthouseFriends says she cared for the lights until 1927; the Township museum says she served 23 years.

keepers.name: Clement E. Richardson
keepers.note: Archive span 1927-1929. The Township museum lists him among the keepers in 'the period 1923-39', which conflicts with the archive and with Anna Garrity's dates.

keepers.name: Vincent Newagon
keepers.note: Named only by the Township museum, after Anna Garrity and before Clement Richardson, with no dates other than 'the period 1923-39'.

keepers.name: Gustav Hansen
keepers.note: Named only by the Township museum, with the same caveat as Newagon.

corrections.why: The Township museum says the range light 'remains an active aid to navigation' and that both lights are under Coast Guard supervision. The USLHS record says 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No', so the USLHS and the museum disagree. The record's 'inactive' rests on the 1967 'deactivated' event (Rowlett's directory), which no source read supports. Confirm against the current Light List before changing.
No source read says the lights were deactivated in 1967. The 1967 change was the replacement of the front tower (HMDB); LighthouseFriends describes the lights as still in service after 1940.

notes_for_editor: (1) Status: the record says inactive (Rowlett: deactivated 1967). The Township museum says the range light remains an active aid, and LighthouseFriends describes the 1940 green light as the current characteristic. The USLHS record says not an active aid. The story reports both and does not settle it; see corrections. (2) First light: HMDB says in operation by August 1870; the Township museum dates service from 1871. The record's 1870 is kept. (3) Keeper dates conflict: the archive has Anna Garrity 1903-1926 and Clement E. Richardson 1927-1929. LighthouseFriends says Anna served until 1927. The Township museum says she served 23 years and places Newagon, Richardson and Hansen in 'the period 1923-39'. Newagon and Hansen appear only in the museum's account. A Lighthouse Digest search snippet (not read in full) says she held the post 'until shortly before her death on May 21, 1937'; that conflicts with every other source and was not used. (4) Bulletin 1915 (PDF page 50) lists 'Presque Isle, Mich.' with keeper 'Thomas Garraty' under 'New Construction'. It is not clear whether this is the range or the main light, so it is not used. (5) Front tower move: HMDB gives 2002 for the move back toward its original site; LighthouseFriends and the Township museum describe moves after the 1995 purchase without a single date. (6) Rear light ownership: LighthouseFriends says privately owned; the Township museum describes the rear light as part of the township park, with the former keeper's house now private. The story reports both without naming any private resident. (7) No storms, wrecks or rescues at the range lights were found in the sources read; the Storms chapter is omitted. The 1884 Life-Saving Service entry for a schooner near 'the old light-house, Presque Isle, Michigan' concerns the older light, not this station. (8) The Lighthouse Board reports for 1870-1889 are not in the corpus, so the 1869-1870 appropriations and construction rest on HMDB, the Township museum and LighthouseFriends. (9) us-mi-presque-isle-range-rear is hidden and merged into this record. (10) Other stations: Patrick and Thomas Garrity served at the New Presque Isle Light (us-mi-new-presque-isle). LighthouseFriends also names Middle Island and St. Clair Flats range lights for Patrick Garrity, but without dates, and those ids were not confirmed, so they are not linked. (11) Privacy: the Township museum and LighthouseFriends mention a private family that tends the Sims grave and private owners of the former keeper's house; neither is named. (12) LighthouseFriends is all-rights-reserved: the story paraphrases it with short quotations only. The HMDB and Township museum texts are quoted in short phrases. (13) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story now paraphrases the museum and LighthouseFriends where it had quoted whole sentences, and keeps one short HMDB quotation per paragraph. Units added: 21 ft (6.4 m), 36 ft (11 m), 500 ft (152 m). (14) The museum and HMDB disagree on the order of the front tower's moves (HMDB: moved near its original site in 2002; museum: first to the entrance of the Old Lighthouse Park, then back into Range Light Park); the story reports the museum's order as the museum's. (15) Keepers 1923-39 (Newagon, Hansen) appear only in the museum's account and are not confirmed by the archive; the story gives them as the museum's list. (16) Rear light ownership: LighthouseFriends says privately owned; the museum places it in the park's parking area. Both are reported in the story. (17) Archive roster lines were checked against roster.py output (Coddington 1870-1875, Sims 1875-1887, Thomas Garrity 1887-1891, Patrick Garrity Sr. 1891-1903, Anna T. Garrity 1903-1926, Clement E. Richardson 1927-1929), and the person slugs match the archive's.
